## CodeQL-gating latency decision — owner disposition

Per the epic AC, the one adopted-practice item that would add **real pre-merge
minutes** to the Gerrit Verified gate is making CodeQL vote-casting (moving
`codeql.yml` from its current `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` triggers onto the
Gerrit refspec as a `vote.needs`).

**Recommendation: keep CodeQL scheduled/non-gating (do NOT add it to the Verified
gate) at this time.**

Rationale, consistent with the epic's central constraint (minimise CI runtime
without weakening confidence in code that passes the gate):
- CodeQL is a full compiled-analysis pass; per-change it is minutes of added
  hot-path latency on every patchset — by far the largest single addition of any
  item considered, and the only one that is not near-zero.
- Its value is regression-detection over the whole tree, which the current
  scheduled run against `origin/main` already provides; a defect it would catch is
  surfaced to the CI owner on the next scheduled sweep rather than escaping silently.
- The gate already carries the cheaper high-signal security layers adopted in this
  epic (S1 zizmor over the vote-path workflows, S2 SHA-pinning), so the marginal
  pre-merge security gain from also gating CodeQL is small relative to its latency.

This is explicitly the **CI owner's call**: if per-change SAST gating is later judged
worth the added minutes (e.g. after the other latency reductions land and leave
headroom), the change is a scoped follow-up — trigger `codeql.yml` on the Gerrit
refspec and add it as a `vote.needs`. Filing that as its own ticket is the adopt
path; leaving CodeQL scheduled is the disposition recorded here.
